$comment: Root ADR-0461. The Seoul front door: an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of each Cloudflare Worker that Korean visitors read, because the Free zone's Cloudflare addresses send KT visitors to LAX and SK Broadband and LG U+ visitors to HKG (W43, measured 2026-11-09), while CloudFront answered at ICN on 12 of 12 Korean probes. infra/cdn/main.tf reads this file, scripts/deploy/edge_settings.py applies it on the data host once the runtime-secrets group aws-cdn exists, and the Workers' wrangler renderers attach origin_hostname as a Worker custom domain. answered_by is the switch: cloudflare keeps the public hostname a Worker custom domain (the Worker deploy attaches it); cloudfront drops it from the Worker and the edge apply makes it a DNS-only CNAME to the distribution. Rollback is setting it back to cloudflare: the next Worker deploy takes the hostname back (Wrangler replaces the CNAME) and the edge apply forgets the record.
price_class_reason: The cheapest class whose edges include South Korea (PriceClass_100 is North America, Europe and Israel only). Korean visitors pay the Korean rate in every class; the class only decides which edges may answer.

origin.reason: 60 s is CloudFront's largest keep-alive without a quota request: the regional edge cache reuses one TLS connection to the Cloudflare edge instead of a handshake per miss. 30 s is CloudFront's default read timeout and above every Worker's answer (the by-PNU latency gate bounds them in seconds).

cache.reason: The origin's Cache-Control decides, and nothing here copies it: the immutable release URLs (tiles, by-PNU generations, media, profiles: public, max-age=31536000, immutable) stay a year, the manifests and the index (no-cache, max-age=0) are asked again every time, the patched tiles and the by-PNU documents, whose answer changes under the same URL, keep their hour in the browser and s-maxage=60 here (root ADR-0470: the seconds their Worker itself holds the manifest that decides them; orchestration/tests/test_cdn_shared_cache_lifetime.py), and an answer without Cache-Control is not stored (default 0). The Workers answer Vary: Origin and refuse an origin they do not list, so Origin and the preflight's two request headers are in the key; no cookie and no query string reaches them (the tile Worker answers 404 to any query, the by-PNU Worker accepts none).

web_preview.caching_reason: The temporary preview (root ADR-0249) is a Next.js app: its answers vary by RSC headers and query strings CloudFront would have to know. It passes every request through uncached (Managed-CachingDisabled with Managed-AllViewerExceptHostHeader) and caches only /_next/static/*, whose names are content hashes. It still gains the Seoul edge and AWS's network to the Cloudflare origin. Its hostname is new, so it never was a Worker custom domain and starts on CloudFront.

budget.name: perfectory-cdn-free-tier
budget.reason: AWS's zero-spend template: the always-free tier (1 TB out and 10 million requests a month) is the whole plan, so the first cent of actual spend mails the identity platform's staff, and a forecast above the limit mails them before the month ends. Email subscribers need no confirmation.
